text:
incident-bot: paging oncall — Dedicated pool 'dp-quanta-east-1' reporting GPU capacity exhaustion for tenant QuantaHealth. 

incident-bot: alerts: gpu_util=98%, gpu_queue_depth=820, tail_latency_95=1200ms, failed_requests=42 (5xx) in last 5m. Affected route: /v1/generate (model: redwood-large-8k).

Alice: I'm on it. grabbing runbook.

Devon: Customer-facing spike — support seeing errors from QuantaHealth's production namespace. Carla, FYI.

Carla: Thanks. I'll prepare an outbound note if we need to enable burst or degrade model. What are mitigation options? :thinking_face:

Bob: Options: 1) enable tenant burst (adds reserved GPUs from shared burst capacity) 2) eviction of background/low-priority tenants on this pool 3) route QuantaHealth to a smaller variant (redwood-medium-8k) with graceful throttling 4) emergency autoscale (add nodes) via infra.

Erin: Autoscaler is at max for this pool right now — there's a 5-min cooldown and cloud quotas might slow new instances. Burst is fastest if quota available. We can also offload to a warm standby in us-west but cross-region latency will increase.

Frank: handoff to Alice — you're primary now. tagging infra: @Erin for burst and autoscale, @Bob for model fallback config, @Carla for customer comms.

Alice: reading exec runbook section 'dedicated-tenant-gpu-exhaustion'. Step 1: attempt burst_override for tenant. If burst fails, Step 2: apply routing fallback to smaller model + rate-limit. Step 3: if still failing, evict least priority containers (coord with infra).

Erin: running check: `infractl pool show dp-quanta-east-1 --quota` -> available_burst_gpus=6.

Alice: good. Initiating burst request now: 
```
infractl pool burst-enable --pool dp-quanta-east-1 --tenant quantahealth --gpus 4 --duration 60m --reason "emergency tenant surge"
```

deploy-bot: burst_enable request accepted (request_id: bstr-20240321-7f9). Provisioning nodes — estimated attach time 3m.

Bob: prepping fallback route. Pushing routing flag to edge: `routes update quantahealth /v1/generate --fallback-model redwood-medium-8k --throttle 20%` — will hold but not flip until Alice approves.

Alice: Approve fallback toggle if burst doesn't reduce queue in 5m. Go ahead but keep it staged.

Erin: nodes attaching. infra logs: "attached 2 g4dn.xlarge equiv GPUs to dp-quanta-east-1". pool gpu_util now 85%, queue_depth 420.

Devon: errors dropping in support stream. Customer calls from QuantaHealth app still show elevated latency but fewer 5xx. Carla — want to ping them with ETA?

Carla: Sending short note: "We are seeing elevated traffic and have enabled emergency capacity while we monitor. Expect stabilization in ~10 minutes; we'll update sooner if anything changes." Sending now.

Alice: monitoring. If queue_depth < 200 and tail_latency_95 < 400ms in next 8m, keep burst for cool-down window and then release. If not, flip fallback and start eviction plan.

Erin: after attach: gpu_util=72%, queue_depth=160, tail_latency_95=380ms. Looks good.

Bob: hold staged route; no flip needed.

Alice: marking incident as mitigation applied. Open action items: (1) postmortem run: identify root cause of spike on QuantaHealth side (sudden batch job?), (2) review pool autoscale thresholds and burst policy, (3) confirm cloud quotas for faster attach.

Carla: QuantaHealth replied — they had a nightly batch that accidentally hit prod earlier than scheduled. They've paused and will throttle job.

Frank: handing back oncall to next shift (Frank -> Alice remains owner for postmortem). If anyone needs further escalation, page oncall. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: incident update: mitigation=burst-enabled(4 GPUs) -> stabilized. incident_state=monitoring.

Alice: closing immediate critical pager. Will file a short incident note and set a postmortem runbook task. Thanks team. :heart:
